ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the left side of the agricultural system shown is a raised "platform field," where crops such as wheat, corn, cotton, soybeans, and sorghum are planted, and there are livestock and poultry such as chickens, pigs, and sheep; the right side is a low-lying "fish pond," with fish cultured in layers in the pond and plankton. The arrows in the figure show the platform field "draining saline water" toward the fish pond, and the bottom of the fish pond being backfilled or improving the platform field through "digging mud"; livestock and poultry manure, crop waste, fish-pond remains, etc. participate in the cycle. Then reason: this "platform field—fish pond" model is suitable for areas with low-lying terrain, easy waterlogging, high groundwater level, and easy salinization, comprehensively controlling drought, flood, salinity, and alkalinity problems by raising platform fields to drain salt and water, using fish ponds to store water and raise fish, and using pond mud to fertilize fields. The typical low-lying waterlogged area in eastern China with relatively prominent salinization and alkalization and suitable for promoting this model is the Huang-Huai-Hai region, namely the North China Plain.
